content: Do not take perindopril if you are pregnant. If you become pregnant while taking perindopril, contact your doctor immediately, as this medication can harm the fetus. Perindopril is prescribed to treat high blood pressure, either alone or in combination with other medications. It belongs to a class of drugs called angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors. It works by relaxing blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more smoothly, by blocking the production of certain natural chemicals that tighten blood vessels. Perindopril is available as an oral tablet and is usually taken once or twice daily. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take perindopril exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it, or take it more frequently than prescribed. Your doctor may start you on a low dose and gradually increase it. Perindopril helps control high blood pressure but does not cure it. Continue taking it even if you feel well, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before taking perindopril, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to perindopril or any other ACE inhibitors, such as benazepril, captopril, enalapril, fosinopril, lisinopril, moexipril, quinapril, ramipril, or trandolapril. Also, inform them about all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Be sure to mention medications such as cyclosporine, diuretics, heparin, indomethacin, lithium, and potassium supplements. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you closely for side effects. Inform your doctor if you are on dialysis or if you have a history of heart failure, lupus, scleroderma, diabetes, angioedema (swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, or extremities), or kidney or liver disease. Additionally, let your doctor know if you plan to become pregnant or are breastfeeding. Be aware that diarrhea, vomiting, dehydration, or excessive sweating can lead to a drop in blood pressure, causing lightheadedness or fainting. Consult your doctor before using salt substitutes containing potassium. If your doctor prescribes a low-salt or low-sodium diet, follow these instructions carefully. If you miss a dose of perindopril, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Perindopril may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: cough, headache, weakness, dizziness, diarrhea, stomach pain, or upset stomach. Some side effects can be serious. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following: swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, or lower legs; hoarseness; difficulty swallowing or breathing; lightheadedness; fainting; fever, sore throat, chills, or other signs of infection; or irregular or rapid heartbeats. If you experience any unusual problems while taking this medication, inform your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store perindopril in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the person has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
